question: How can beings think anything here if everything depends on the established principle of consciousness-unity?
premises: Beings do not think anything here independently.
All cognition depends on that underlying principle.
The principle of consciousness-unity is already established.
inference: The possibility of thinking must be explained from the established unity of consciousness.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'that' in 'depending-on-that' is not explicit in this verse alone.
plain_english: They do not really think anything here on their own, because everything depends on that. How is this so? Listen: it is because the principle of the unity of consciousness is firmly established.
